title: The Higgs hierarchy problem: why the weak scale is so light
bottleneck: Quantum corrections should drag the Higgs mass up toward the Planck scale, yet it sits at 125 GeV, requiring cancellations precise to roughly one part in 10^34 between the bare mass and loop contributions. No symmetry of the Standard Model protects a fundamental scalar's mass the way chiral and gauge symmetries protect fermions and bosons.
why_it_blocks: The hierarchy problem was the primary theoretical motivation for decades of beyond-Standard-Model physics; its persistence means the Standard Model's most basic mass scale is unexplained and possibly fine-tuned.
current_state: Supersymmetry, composite Higgs, and extra dimensions have all been pushed to fine-tuned territory by LHC null results, reviving interest in anthropic, cosmological-relaxation, and 'unnatural' explanations. Cosmological relaxation and N-naturalness attempt dynamical explanations, while others accept fine-tuning as evidence for a multiverse.
